title.rendered: Lazarus, Come Forth | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 11

excerpt.rendered: A sealed tomb outside Bethany. A four-day-old corpse inside. The prayer that came out of Jesus was not a request. It was a thanksgiving for an answered prayer, followed by a direct command.

content.rendered:
A sealed tomb outside Bethany. A four-day-old corpse inside. The grieving sister standing beside Jesus. And the prayer that came out of Him in that hour was not a request. It was a thanksgiving for an answered prayer that had not yet manifested, followed by a direct command to a dead body. This is how a Son of God prays.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, October 13, 2026 | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 11

Today’s Scripture

“Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead man was lying. And Jesus lifted up His eyes and said, ‘Father, I thank You that You have heard Me. And I know that You always hear Me, but because of the people who are standing by I said this, that they may believe that You sent Me.’ Now when He had said these things, He cried with a loud voice, ‘Lazarus, come forth!'”
John 11:41-43 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Jesus arrived at Bethany four days after Lazarus had died. Jewish tradition believed the spirit lingered near the body for three days. By the fourth day, there was no ambiguity. The body was decomposing. Martha said as much when Jesus asked for the stone to be rolled away. “Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days.” Jesus had deliberately waited. He had waited for the situation to become humanly impossible, so that what was about to happen could not be explained by any natural cause. And then, standing in front of a sealed tomb with a public crowd watching, Jesus prayed one of the most instructive prayers in the whole New Testament. In two movements. The first movement was a thanksgiving for an answer that had not yet manifested in the natural realm. The second movement was a direct command to a dead body.

This is not how most believers pray. Most believers pray by begging God to do something. By pleading for a change. By trying to persuade a reluctant Father to act. Jesus prayed from a different place entirely. He prayed as a Son who already knew the Father’s heart, already had the Father’s authority, and already knew the answer was yes before He opened His mouth. The Passion Translation captures His confidence: “Jesus gazed into heaven and said, ‘Father, thank you that you have heard my prayer, for I know that you always listen to me, but I’m saying this for the benefit of all these people standing here, so that they will believe that you have sent me.’ After he prayed, Jesus shouted with a loud voice, ‘Lazarus! Come out of the tomb!'” (John 11:41-43 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “Father, I thank You that You have heard Me. Yes, I know You always hear and listen to Me” (John 11:41-42 AMPC). Always hear and listen. Jesus prayed from assurance, not from anxiety.

How Jesus Prayed

The Format. Two movements, nothing else. First, a thanksgiving directed upward to the Father for an answer already given. Second, a command directed outward to the circumstance. No pleading. No lengthy preamble. No religious vocabulary. Just thanks, then speak.

The Essence. Jesus thanked the Father before the dead man walked out. The thanksgiving was not for what He hoped would happen. It was for what He knew had already been granted in heaven. He then released the already-granted answer into the earth by commanding the circumstance to come into alignment with it. Heaven first. Earth second.

The Authority. Jesus did not ask the Father to raise Lazarus. He did not request. He did not beg. He commanded. “Lazarus, come forth!” The command was spoken with a loud voice, in front of a crowd, to a four-day-old corpse. The authority belonged to Him as the Son, and He used it. He did not try to persuade the Father to use authority on His behalf. He exercised the authority He already had.

The Assurance. “I know that You always hear Me.” There was no doubt in the prayer. No “if it be Your will.” No hedging. Jesus knew the Father’s will and spoke from certain knowledge. This is not presumption. This is the assurance of a Son who lives in constant communion with the Father and knows what He has already granted.

The Submission. Here is the critical balance. Jesus explicitly said “because of the people who are standing by I said this, that they may believe that You sent Me.” The authority was not for Jesus’ own display. It was submitted to the Father’s purpose — that people would believe. True authority in prayer is always submitted authority. It is exercised to accomplish the Father’s agenda, not the believer’s ego.

The Result. A four-day-old corpse walked out of the tomb, grave clothes trailing. Many of the Jews who had come to mourn with Mary believed on Him that day. The miracle served the mission, exactly as Jesus had said it would. And the authority with which Jesus spoke to the tomb is the same authority He has placed on the believer. “He who believes in Me, the works that I do he will do also; and greater works than these he will do, because I go to My Father” (John 14:12 NKJV).

This is the heart of New Testament prayer. The believer does not beg God to change circumstances. The believer thanks the Father for what has already been accomplished at the cross, and then speaks to the circumstance. The believer does not plead with God to heal — the believer speaks healing to the body. The believer does not beg God to calm the storm — the believer speaks peace to the storm, as Jesus did in Mark 4:39. The believer does not beg God for provision — the believer thanks the Father for the provision Jesus already purchased, and declares it into manifestation. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, learn to pray as Jesus prayed. Thank the Father before the answer manifests. Then speak to the circumstance in His name. The authority is yours in Christ.

Prayer (Pattern After Jesus)

Address and Thanksgiving (upward). Father, I thank You that You have heard me. I thank You that in Christ the answer has already been granted. The work was finished at the cross. I live in the finished work.

Command (outward, to the situation). In the name of Jesus, I speak to [name the situation — the sickness, the mountain, the lack, the fear, the closed door]. I command you to come into alignment with the Father’s finished work in Christ. Be removed. Be healed. Be opened. Be subdued.

Submission. Not for my glory, Father, but that Your name will be known in my life, and that those around me will believe that You sent Jesus.

In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I pray with the authority Jesus modelled. I thank the Father before the manifestation. I speak to the circumstance in the name of Jesus. My words carry Spirit-authority because the One who gave them to me is seated at the right hand of the Father.
